title: Grateful Dead Live at Grand Prix Racecourse on 1973-07-27
lineage: SBD> Master Reel (but see note)> Dat (48k)> Dat (Sony D8)> RME Hammerfall Digiface> Sony Vaio C1VP> Samplitude v7.02 Professional> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of the legendary Watkins Glen 1973 sound‑check, highlighted by an epic Jam → Wharf Rat that even hints at Fire on the Mountain.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑sourced soundboard upgrade delivers an exceptionally clean and detailed recording, letting listeners hear every nuance of Keith’s electric tapping and Phil’s “insane” bass work. While the song renditions are brief and a bit perfunctory, the 20‑minute jam (Bird Song into Wharf Rat) is universally praised as one of the finest pre‑1974 Dead jams. Overall the performance radiates high energy and tight improvisation despite being a sound‑check.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 5) and enthusiastic comments about both the musical peak (the jam) and superb soundboard quality drive a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Upgraded Miller soundboard mix; described as crystal‑clear, crisp, and ‘as clear as day’ with no noted dropouts or muffiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A brief sound‑check set that turned into an impromptu concert; song structures are loose, but the extended jam provides a cohesive and thrilling centerpiece.

band_member_comments.Phil: Phil is described as ‘absolutely insane’ on bass during the jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s electric tapping in the jam is highlighted as a soaring, dragon‑like moment.
